The best art style and art direction I've ever seen in a game. The combat is so satisfying that even if you rage quit, you'll probably come back to it because no other game compares. And somehow there isn't a single bad voice performance across all 29 characters.

My only complaint is that you really start to notice how poorly balanced the game is after a few successful escapes--and when you have to start cranking up heat levels in order to go for 100%, your average player will have to rely pretty hard on RNG in order to get any viable run.

8/10

Everything that can be said about Hades already has been - an rocking soundtrack, impressive story, fun characterizations of the gods, ridiculous customization are all inarguable assets in its favor. My addition to the discourse is pointing out its welcome contribution to the roguelite genre - your progress is not beholden to the whims of fate and being necessarily screwed out of a victory by a "bad run". While certain boons are certainly more or less synergestic with themselves/your loadout, Hades shines in that it allows for skill to make up the randomness gap - you aren't entirely reliant on drawing a particular card combination or an enemy dishing out unavoidable damage. Proper positioning, timing, and skill can overcome many suboptimal boon pairings.
I would also be remiss not to call attention to the Heat system - the degree of customization one gets in increasing run difficulty is something to be emulated.
Do yourself a favor and play this game. (And remember, when you first beat it, you haven't, actually).

Despite its age, Hades is still a top contender for one of the best roguelikes especially for its niche and how well-made it is despite comparison to newer games. Hades somehow blends combat, storyline (as expected of any game) but also romance perfectly and believe me when i say that you'll be disappointed you couldnt find any other game that could achieve the same result without it getting corny or feeling like it's a drop in quality.

my own review after 30+ runs is that the combat doesnt get too repetitive even if you run the same weapon for all of your runs like i do with the shield.. there's a whole bunch of options to choose from (duos boons, cast/special builds) and the next run will never feel like the last, despite similar choices. There are also rewarding upgrades the more runs you do, though it gets repetitive if you play only for the roguelike, which is where the story and thanatos walks in.

I wont go too much into detail but im a sucker for cute relationships and i also enjoy the option of having meg as a romance option so i can decline. It is very very motivating knowing there's this death incarnate dude trying to impress you on random runs, and YES we're all equipping his keepsake. The storyline may be a tiny bit lackluster for some as it's locked behind dozens of runs and is fairly simple, the attractiveness of it is determined by how interested you are towards the characters and whether the combat makes up for it or not (which imo it does, the combat is enjoyable and so are the bonds you get to build with than or meg.)

tdlr; normal to good replayability, good character building and story, memorable sound design and decent voice acting, an insanely good introduction to roguelike as someone who's never played these games, thanatos.
